title: Sri Maha Bodhi planted
description: A cutting of the tree under which the Buddha attained enlightenment is planted at Anuradhapura, and it is still growing there.

title: Buddhism comes to the island
description: By tradition the monk Mahinda, son of Ashoka, meets King Devanampiya Tissa on the hill of Mihintale and converts him to Buddhism.

title: Dutugamunu defeats Elara
description: The Sinhalese prince Dutugamunu kills the Chola-born king Elara and rules the whole island from Anuradhapura.

title: Pali Canon written down
description: Monks commit the Buddhist scriptures to writing for the first time, after centuries of oral transmission.

title: Sigiriya rock fortress
description: King Kashyapa builds a palace and gardens on and around a 200-metre rock, which he makes his capital.

title: Chola invasion
description: Rajaraja I of the Chola Empire invades and sacks Anuradhapura, ending its thirteen centuries as the capital.

title: Vijayabahu I drives out the Cholas
description: Vijayabahu ends Chola rule and reunites the island with Polonnaruwa as its capital.

title: Parakramabahu I becomes king
description: Parakramabahu the Great begins a reign known for large reservoirs, the rebuilding of Polonnaruwa and the reform of the Buddhist order.

title: Invasion of Kalinga Magha
description: Magha of Kalinga takes Polonnaruwa, after which the Sinhalese kings move south-west and the old dry-zone cities are abandoned.

title: Ming–Kotte War
description: The Chinese admiral Zheng He defeats and captures the ruler Alakeshvara and carries him to the Ming court.

title: Portuguese arrive
description: A fleet under Lourenço de Almeida reaches the island, the beginning of four and a half centuries of European involvement.

title: Campaign of Danture
description: Vimaladharmasuriya I destroys a Portuguese army invading the highlands, securing the independence of the Kingdom of Kandy.

title: Portuguese conquest of Jaffna
description: Portugal annexes the Tamil kingdom of the north and executes its last king, Cankili II.

title: Kandyan Treaty with the Dutch
description: King Rajasinghe II allies with the Dutch East India Company to drive out the Portuguese.

title: Dutch take Colombo
description: The Portuguese garrison surrenders after a seven-month siege, and the Dutch keep the coast instead of handing it to Kandy.

title: British take Colombo
description: The Dutch surrender their possessions on the island to a British force, and the coast becomes a British colony.

title: Kandyan Convention
description: Kandyan chiefs depose their king and cede the kingdom to Britain, ending the last independent state on the island.

title: Uva rebellion
description: Kandyan chiefs rise against British rule and are put down with the destruction of villages and crops in Uva.

title: First tea estate
description: James Taylor plants the first commercial tea on the island, and tea replaces coffee as the main export after a leaf disease ruins the coffee estates.

title: Riots of 1915
description: Clashes between Sinhalese Buddhists and Muslims spread across the island, and the harsh British response spurs the nationalist movement.

title: Universal suffrage
description: The Donoughmore Constitution gives the vote to all adults, men and women, the first such grant in a British colony in Asia.

title: Easter Sunday Raid
description: Japanese carrier aircraft bomb Colombo harbour and sink two British cruisers at sea.

title: Independence
description: Ceylon becomes a self-governing dominion with D. S. Senanayake as its first prime minister.

title: Sinhala Only Act
description: Parliament makes Sinhala the sole official language, a measure opposed by Tamils and followed by riots.

title: Sirimavo Bandaranaike becomes prime minister
description: The widow of the assassinated S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike becomes the first woman in the world to head an elected government.

title: JVP insurrection
description: The Marxist Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna attacks police stations across the south in a youth uprising that is crushed within weeks.

title: Republic of Sri Lanka
description: A new constitution makes the country a republic, changes its name from Ceylon and gives Buddhism the foremost place.

title: Black July
description: After Tamil Tigers kill thirteen soldiers near Jaffna, mobs kill hundreds or thousands of Tamils, the start of a civil war lasting 26 years.

title: Indo-Sri Lanka Accord
description: Sri Lanka agrees to devolve power to provinces and India sends a peacekeeping force to the north, which ends up fighting the Tamil Tigers.

title: Ceasefire agreement
description: The government and the Tamil Tigers sign a ceasefire brokered by Norway, which holds for some years before the war resumes.

title: End of the civil war
description: The army overruns the last territory of the Tamil Tigers and kills their leader Velupillai Prabhakaran.

title: Easter bombings
description: Suicide bombers linked to Islamic State attack three churches and three hotels, killing about 270 people.
